questions.question: Which of the following metals is most ductile?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gold** is the most ductile metal known to mankind, meaning it can be drawn into extremely thin wires without breaking.
 
• It is possible to draw a single gram of gold into a wire with a length of approximately **2.4 kilometers**.
 
• The exceptional **ductility** of gold is due to its **metallic bonding,** where electrons are free to move, allowing atoms to slide past each other without breaking the structure.
 
• Gold is widely used in **electrical wiring, jewelry, and decorative items** due to its ductility and other properties such as **resistance to corrosion** and **excellent conductivity.**
 
• Its ability to be shaped into intricate designs makes it invaluable in industries such as **electronics** and **aerospace.**
 
• Gold is also highly valued for its **economic and cultural significance** across the globe, often symbolizing wealth and prosperity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sodium**__

 __
 
• **Sodium** is a highly reactive alkali metal and is not known for its ductility.
 
• It is soft and can be cut with a knife, but its **low melting point** and reactivity make it unsuitable for applications requiring ductility.
 
• Sodium is primarily used in **chemical industries** and in the production of **sodium compounds** like sodium hydroxide and table salt.
 
 
 
• **Lithium**__
 __
 
• **Lithium** is the lightest metal and is moderately ductile, but it does not compare to gold in terms of ductility.
 
• It is widely used in **batteries**, especially in **lithium-ion batteries**, due to its high energy density.
 
• Other applications include **ceramics, glass manufacturing, and as a mood-stabilizing drug in medicine.**
 
 
 
• **Lead**__
 
 
• **Lead** is a soft and malleable metal, but it is far less ductile than gold.
 
• It is primarily used in **batteries (lead-acid batteries)**, radiation shielding, and in the production of **alloys and pipes.**
 
• Lead has a high density and is toxic, limiting its use in certain industries.

questions.question: At what rate (in percentage) per annum will ₹1,300 give ₹650 as simple interest in 10 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1,300

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹650

Time (t) = 10 years

**Formula used:**

SI = P × R × T / 100

Where, R = rate

**Calculations:**

650 = 1300 × R × 10 / 100

⇒ 650 = 13000R / 100

⇒ 650 = 130R

⇒ R = 650 / 130

⇒ R = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: Asexual reproduction does NOT involve the formation of ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**zygotes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Asexual reproduction does not involve the formation of **zygotes**, as it is a process that occurs without the fusion of gametes.
 
• In asexual reproduction, a single parent reproduces offspring that are genetically identical, as there is no mixing of genetic material.
 
• **Zygote** formation is characteristic of **sexual reproduction**, where male and female gametes fuse to form a diploid cell.
 
• Examples of organisms that reproduce asexually include **amoeba, bacteria, hydra, and certain plants like bryophytes**.
 
• Methods of asexual reproduction include **budding, binary fission, fragmentation, spore formation, and vegetative propagation**.
 
• Asexual reproduction is advantageous as it enables rapid reproduction in stable environments and ensures the perpetuation of successful genetic traits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Buds**__

 __
 
• **Budding** is a type of asexual reproduction where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• Examples include **hydra and yeast**, where the bud eventually detaches to become an independent organism.
 
 
 
• **Spore**__
 __
 
• **Spore formation** is another mode of asexual reproduction, commonly seen in fungi, algae, and some non-flowering plants like mosses and ferns.
 
• It involves the production of **spores**, which are reproductive units capable of developing into a new organism under favorable conditions.
 
 
 
• **Leaves**__
 
 
• In certain plants, asexual reproduction can occur through **vegetative propagation**, where new plants grow from leaves.
 
• For instance, the plant **Bryophyllum** reproduces asexually when plantlets grow along the edges of its leaves.

questions.question: If a stone is thrown up, the value of acceleration due to gravity ‘g’ will be taken as _______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Negative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a stone is thrown upward, the direction of motion is opposite to the direction of **gravitational force.**
 
• The acceleration due to gravity (**g**) always acts in the downward direction, i.e., towards the center of the Earth.
 
• In this scenario, since the upward motion of the stone is opposite to the direction of gravity, the value of **g** becomes **negative**.
 
• The negative sign indicates the opposing direction of the gravitational force relative to the motion of the object.
 
• As the stone rises, its velocity decreases due to the negative acceleration until it reaches the highest point, where the velocity becomes **zero.**
 
• Once the stone starts to fall back down, the acceleration due to gravity acts in the same direction as its motion, and the value of **g** becomes **positive.**
 
• This principle is based on the laws of motion and Newton’s universal law of gravitation.
 
• Understanding the sign convention of **g** is crucial for solving various problems in physics, such as projectile motion, free fall, and other kinematic calculations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Infinite**__

 __
 
• The term **infinite** is not applicable in this context as the acceleration due to gravity (**g**) has a fixed value near the Earth's surface, approximately **9.8 m/s².**
 
• **Infinity** generally refers to an unbounded or limitless value, which does not describe gravitational acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Zero**__
 __
 
• The value of **g** cannot be **zero** as long as the object is within the influence of Earth's gravity.
 
• **Zero gravitational acceleration** would only occur in deep space, far away from any massive object exerting a gravitational pull.
 
 
 
• **Positive**__
 
 
• The value of **g** is considered **positive** when the motion of the object is in the same direction as the gravitational force.
 
• In this case, when the stone is falling back down, the acceleration due to gravity becomes **positive.**

questions.question: Which of the following has two ends: one which is hydrophilic and the other which is hydrophobic?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Soap**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soap** is a substance that has a dual nature - a **hydrophilic (water-attracting) end** and a **hydrophobic (water-repelling) end.**
 
• The hydrophilic end of soap is attracted to **water molecules**, making it soluble in water.
 
• The hydrophobic end is attracted to **oil, grease, and dirt**, helping to remove these substances from surfaces.
 
• When soap is mixed with water, it forms structures called **micelles**, where the hydrophobic ends trap grease and dirt, while the hydrophilic ends remain in water, helping to wash away impurities.
 
• Soap is widely used in **cleaning, personal hygiene, and industrial processes** due to its amphiphilic properties.
 
• Soap is made through a process called **saponification**, where fats or oils are reacted with an alkali, such as sodium hydroxide or potassium hydroxide.
 
• Examples of soap products include **bar soap, liquid soap, and detergent powders**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Water**__

 __
 
• **Water** is a universal solvent but does not have amphiphilic properties like soap.
 
• It is composed of **hydrogen and oxygen (H₂O)** and forms hydrogen bonds with other water molecules.
 
• It is essential for life and is used in **drinking, agriculture, industry, and sanitation**.
 
 
 
• **Perfume**__
 __
 
• **Perfume** is a mixture of fragrant essential oils or aroma compounds, solvents, and fixatives used to create a pleasant smell.
 
• It does not have hydrophilic or hydrophobic ends and is insoluble in water.
 
• Perfumes are primarily used in **personal care products** and for aromatherapy.
 
 
 
• **Cream**__
 
 
• **Cream** is an emulsion of water and fat and is used in **cosmetics, skincare, and food products**.
 
• While it contains both water and oil, it does not exhibit the dual hydrophilic and hydrophobic properties of soap.
 
• Cream products are used for **hydration, moisturization, and cooking.**

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the relationship between u(object distance), v (image distance) and f (focal length) of a spherical mirror?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**(1/v) + (1/u) = (1/f)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• This equation is known as the **Mirror Formula**, which establishes a relationship between the **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** for a spherical mirror.
 
• The formula is applicable for both **concave** and **convex mirrors**.
 
• In the equation, all distances are measured from the **pole of the mirror**, and the **sign convention** must be followed to determine the nature of the distances (positive or negative).
 
• **Concave mirrors** form real and inverted images for objects placed beyond the focal point and virtual images when the object is within the focal length.
 
• **Convex mirrors**, however, always produce virtual, erect, and diminished images regardless of the object’s position.
 
• The formula is derived from the geometry of the mirror and is used in various applications, including **optics, imaging systems, and physics experiments**.
 
• The equation ensures the quantitative analysis of image formation, allowing scientists and engineers to calculate the exact position and size of the image.

questions.question:
Given below is a cause followed by possible effects numbered I, II and III. Read the cause carefully and decide which of the three can be a/the possible effect(s).

Cause:

Heavy rains and flash floods have inundated many low lying areas of City X.

Effects:

(I) The State Government has appointed a new head for the municipality of City X.

(II) The State Government has evacuated over 5500 people stranded in low lying areas of City X.

(III) Food and water is being distributed at multiple locations to help citizens who have been evacuated from City X.

options.text: Both II and III can be the possible effects
Only I can be a possible effect
Only II can be a possible effect
Both I and II can be the possible effects

questions.solution:
**Given cause:** Heavy rains and flash floods have inundated many low lying areas of City X.

**Given effects:**

(I) The State Government has appointed a new head for the municipality of City X. → Not possible

As mismanagement during the flood could lead to a leadership change but this is not an immediate or guaranteed effect of the disaster itself. 

(II) The State Government has evacuated over 5500 people stranded in low lying areas of City X. → Possible

When floods occur, authorities often evacuate people from affected areas for safety. The given cause mentions that low lying areas were inundated, making evacuation necessary.

(III) Food and water is being distributed at multiple locations to help citizens who have been evacuated from City X. → Possible

After being displaced, people require basic necessities such as food and water. Disaster relief efforts typically involve such measures, making this a possible and reasonable effect.

Thus, **Both II and III can be the possible effects.**

Hence, **"Option 1"** is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following shows Tyndall effect?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Colloids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tyndall effect** refers to the scattering of light by particles in a medium, making the path of light visible.
 
• **Colloids** are mixtures where the particle size ranges between **1 nm to 1000 nm**, large enough to scatter light.
 
• When a beam of light passes through a colloidal solution, the light is scattered, and this phenomenon is called the **Tyndall effect**.
 
• Examples of colloids include **fog, milk, smoke, and gelatin solutions**.
 
• The particles in a colloid are dispersed in a continuous medium and are not visible to the naked eye, but their effect on light is noticeable.
 
• The visibility of the light beam in colloids demonstrates the presence of dispersed particles, proving the heterogeneous nature of colloids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solutions**__

 __
 
• **Solutions** are homogeneous mixtures where the particle size is smaller than **1 nm**.
 
• Due to their small particle size, they do not scatter light and hence do not show the **Tyndall effect**.
 
• Examples of solutions include **sugar water, salt water, and vinegar.**
 
 
 
• **Metals**__
 __
 
• **Metals** are solid substances with a characteristic luster and high electrical and thermal conductivity.
 
• They are not mixtures or dispersions and do not exhibit the **Tyndall effect**.
 
• Examples of metals include **iron, gold, silver, and copper.**
 
 
 
• **Gases**__
 
 
• **Gases** are composed of particles that are widely spaced and move freely.
 
• Pure gases do not exhibit the **Tyndall effect** as their particles are too small to scatter light significantly.
 
• Examples of gases include **oxygen, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide.**

questions.question: A spherical mirror, whose reflecting surface faces towards the centre of the sphere, is called a _______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Concave Mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a spherical mirror whose **reflecting surface faces towards the centre of the sphere**.
 
• It is also known as a **converging mirror** because it reflects light inward toward a focal point.
 
• The principal applications of concave mirrors include their use in **telescopes, headlights, shaving mirrors, and dental mirrors**, where a magnified image is required.
 
• Concave mirrors are capable of forming both **real and virtual images** depending on the position of the object.
 
• The focal length of a concave mirror is half the radius of curvature, denoted mathematically as **f = R/2**.
 
• They are widely used in scientific instruments due to their ability to focus light accurately.
 
• Concave mirrors are also used in **solar concentrators** to focus sunlight for generating heat or energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Plano-convex Mirror**__

 __
 
• Plano-convex mirrors have a flat surface on one side and a convex surface on the other.
 
• They are not spherical mirrors but are typically used in **optical systems** for focusing or collimating light.
 
• These mirrors are mainly used in **lasers, imaging systems, and optical instruments.**
 
 
 
• **Plane Mirror**__
 __
 
• A plane mirror has a **flat reflecting surface**.
 
• It reflects light to form a virtual image that is **upright and of the same size as the object.**
 
• Plane mirrors are commonly used in **bathrooms, dressing tables, and optical setups.**
 
• They do not have the capability to converge or diverge light.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror**__
 
 
• A convex mirror is a spherical mirror whose **reflecting surface bulges outward.**
 
• It is also known as a **diverging mirror** because it spreads light outward.

__
 
• **Milk** is, in fact, a **colloidal solution**, not a non-colloidal solution as mentioned in the question.
 
• A colloidal solution is a **heterogeneous mixture** where one substance is dispersed evenly throughout another.
 
• In milk, fat globules are dispersed in water, making it an example of an **emulsion**, which is a type of colloidal solution.
 
• The particles in colloidal solutions, such as milk, are so small that they do not settle down and cannot be separated by ordinary filtration methods.

• Examples of colloidal solutions include **fog, smoke, and milk.**

• Specialized methods like **ultrafiltration** are required to separate colloidal particles.

• Mathematically, the relationship between gravity and distance can be expressed as **g ∝ 1/r²**, where r is the radius of the Earth at a given location.

• These differences may provide certain individuals with a **survival advantage**, especially when environmental conditions change.
 
• This mechanism leads to **natural selection**, which ensures that favorable traits are passed on to future generations.
 
• For example, the development of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is an outcome of **genetic variation** and selection pressure.

questions.question: At what temperature does water transform into steam under normal atmospheric pressure?

• This process is called **boiling**, and it occurs when the **vapor pressure** of water equals the atmospheric pressure.
 
• At the boiling point, water molecules gain enough **kinetic energy** to overcome intermolecular forces and transition from the **liquid phase to the gaseous phase.**
 
• The boiling point of water can vary depending on **altitude and pressure**. At higher altitudes where pressure is lower, water boils at a temperature below **100ºC**.
 
• This temperature is widely used in **science, cooking, and industrial applications** to measure and control heat processes.
 
• The boiling point of water is a crucial reference point in the **Celsius temperature scale**, where it is defined as **100ºC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

 __

• Water at this temperature is considered hot and is often used in **cooking or beverage preparation**, like making tea or coffee.
 
• At this temperature, water may begin to exhibit signs of **evaporation**, but it does not boil or turn into steam under normal atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: Which part of the flower grows and ripens to form a fruit?

__
 
• The **ovary** is the part of a flower that develops into a fruit after fertilization.
 
• It is located at the base of the pistil, which is the **female reproductive structure** of the flower.
 
• Inside the ovary, there are one or more **ovules**, which contain the egg cells.
 
• After pollination, the **pollen grains** fertilize the ovules, leading to the formation of seeds.
 
• Once fertilization occurs, the ovary undergoes changes and ripens into a fruit, which helps in **seed dispersal.**
 
• The fruit can be fleshy or dry, depending on the type of plant.
 
• Examples of fruits formed from ripened ovaries include **apples, mangoes, and tomatoes.**
 
• This process is essential for the reproduction and propagation of flowering plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• Petals are the **colorful parts** of a flower that attract pollinators such as bees, butterflies, and birds.
 
• They do not play a direct role in the formation of fruits but are crucial for **pollination.**
 
• Petals are part of the flower's corolla and act as a protective layer for the reproductive organs of the flower.
 
 
 
• **Pollen Tube**__
 __
 
• The pollen tube is a structure that forms after a pollen grain lands on the stigma of a flower.
 
• It facilitates the transfer of **male gametes** from the pollen grain to the ovule.

questions.question: Burning of unsaturated compounds gives which of the following?

__
 
• When **unsaturated compounds** such as alkenes and alkynes undergo combustion, they generally produce a **yellow flame**.
 
• The **yellow flame** is caused by the incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons, which leads to the formation of **soot particles**.
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain **double or triple bonds** between carbon atoms, which require more oxygen for complete combustion compared to saturated hydrocarbons.
 
• Due to insufficient oxygen supply during burning, the combustion is incomplete, resulting in the **release of carbon particles** that glow yellow when heated.
 
• Examples of unsaturated hydrocarbons include **ethylene (C₂H₄) and acetylene (C₂H₂).**
 
• The yellow flame is often observed in laboratory experiments when burning hydrocarbons with limited oxygen availability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Green Flame**__

 __
 
• A **green flame** is not typically produced by the combustion of hydrocarbons. It is usually observed when certain **elements like copper or boron compounds** burn, as these elements emit green light due to their specific emission spectra.
 
• For example, the combustion of **copper salts** in a flame produces a green color.
 
 
 
• **Red Flame**__
 __
 
• A **red flame** is associated with the combustion of certain elements like **strontium or lithium compounds**.
 
• It is not related to the burning of hydrocarbons, whether saturated or unsaturated.
 
 
 
• **Clean Flame**__
 
 
• A **clean flame** is typically produced by the complete combustion of **saturated hydrocarbons** like methane or propane.
 
• Complete combustion occurs when there is a sufficient supply of oxygen, resulting in no soot and the production of **carbon dioxide and water vapor.**

questions.question: What happens to the motion of an object when balanced forces act on it?

options.text: Its state of motion remains unchanged.
It changes its direction of motion.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Its state of motion remains unchanged.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Balanced forces are forces that are **equal in magnitude** but act in **opposite directions**.
 
• When balanced forces act on an object, the **net force** becomes zero.
 
• An object remains in its current state of motion (either at rest or in uniform motion) when **no net force** acts on it, as per Newton's **First Law of Motion**.
 
• This phenomenon is often referred to as the **law of inertia**, which states that an object will continue in its existing state unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
 
• For example, if a book is lying on a table and balanced forces act on it (gravity and the table's upward force), the book remains stationary.
 
• Similarly, if an object is moving in a straight line with constant speed and balanced forces act on it, its motion remains **unchanged**.
 
• Balanced forces do not cause any **acceleration**, change in direction, or deformation of the object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It changes its direction of motion.**__

 __
 
• Forces can change the direction of motion, but this happens only when the forces are **unbalanced**, not balanced.
 
• Unbalanced forces produce a **net force** that can alter the trajectory of the object.
 
 
 
• **It speeds up.**__
 __
 
• An object speeds up when unbalanced forces act on it, causing **acceleration**.
 
• Balanced forces do not lead to any change in the **speed or velocity** of an object.
 
 
 
• **It slows down.**__
 
 
• Slowing down or deceleration occurs due to unbalanced forces, such as **friction** or resistance.
 
• Balanced forces cannot decrease an object's speed because there is no net force acting on it.

questions.question: The displacement of a body is perpendicular to the direction in which the force is applied; the work done in this case will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Work done is determined by the formula: **W = F × d × cos(θ)**, where:

 
 
• **W** is the work done,
 
• **F** is the magnitude of the force applied,
 
• **d** is the displacement of the object,
 
• **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement.
 
 
 
• When the **displacement** is perpendicular to the direction of the **force**, the angle **θ** becomes 90 degrees.
 
• The **cosine of 90 degrees** is equal to **0**. Hence, the work done (W) becomes **0**, regardless of the magnitude of force or displacement.
 
• This is because there is **no component of force** acting in the direction of the displacement when the two are perpendicular.
 
• Examples of such cases include:
 
 
• Carrying a bag horizontally while walking forward – the force exerted (vertically upward) by the arms is perpendicular to the horizontal displacement.
 
• Motion of a satellite in a circular orbit – the force (gravitational) is perpendicular to the displacement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Infinite**__

 __
 
• The term **infinite work** is not applicable in real-world physics as it defies the laws of energy conservation.
 
• Work is always a finite quantity, based on the force applied and the displacement.
 
 
 
• **Positive**__
 __
 
• Work is considered **positive** when the force and displacement are in the **same direction**.
 
• For example, pushing a box forward applies a force in the direction of displacement, resulting in positive work.
 
 
 
• **Negative**__
 
 
• Work is considered **negative** when the force and displacement are in **opposite directions**.
 
• For instance, when braking a car, the frictional force acts in the opposite direction to the car's displacement, resulting in negative work.

questions.question: Organisms whose cells lack a nuclear membrane are called _______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**prokaryotes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prokaryotes** are organisms whose cells lack a well-defined **nuclear membrane**, meaning their genetic material is not enclosed within a nucleus.
 
• Their genetic material, usually in the form of a single circular **DNA molecule**, floats freely in a region called the **nucleoid**.
 
• **Prokaryotic cells** are simpler in structure and lack membrane-bound organelles such as the nucleus, mitochondria, and Golgi apparatus.
 
• Examples of **prokaryotic organisms** include **bacteria** (e.g., Escherichia coli) and **archaea** (e.g., Halobacterium).
 
• The absence of a nuclear membrane allows prokaryotes to carry out cellular processes efficiently as their genetic material is easily accessible for replication and transcription.
 
• Prokaryotes are generally smaller in size (usually ranging from **0.1 to 5 micrometers**) compared to eukaryotic cells.
 
• They reproduce primarily through an asexual process called **binary fission**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eukaryotes**__

 __
 
• **Eukaryotic cells** possess a well-defined nucleus enclosed by a **nuclear membrane**.
 
• They contain membrane-bound organelles such as **mitochondria, chloroplasts, and the endoplasmic reticulum**.
 
• Examples of eukaryotic organisms include **plants, animals, fungi, and protists**.
 
• Eukaryotic cells are generally larger in size, ranging from **10 to 100 micrometers**.
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm**__
 __
 
• The **cytoplasm** is the gel-like substance inside the cell where various cellular components and organelles are suspended.
 
• It plays a crucial role in facilitating **cellular processes** such as growth, metabolism, and replication.
 
 
 
• **Chromatin**__
 
 
• **Chromatin** is the complex of **DNA and proteins** found in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
 
• It condenses to form chromosomes during cell division.

questions.question: Nine men went to a restaurant. Eight of them spent Rs. 3 each on their meals and the ninth spent Rs. 2 more than the average expenditure of all the nine. Determine the total money spent by them.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Eight men spent Rs. 3 each

The ninth man spent Rs. 2 more than the average expenditure of all the nine men

**Formula used:**

Average expenditure = Total expenditure / Number of people

Total expenditure = Sum of individual expenditures

**Calculations:**

Total expenditure of eight men = 8 × 3 = Rs. 24

Let the total expenditure of all nine men be Rs. X

Average expenditure of all nine men = X / 9

Expenditure of the ninth man = X / 9 + 2

Sum of expenditures = Total expenditure

⇒ 24 + X / 9 + 2 = X

⇒ 26 + X / 9 = X

⇒ 26 = X - X / 9

⇒ 26 = 8X / 9

⇒ 26 × 9 = 8X

⇒ 234 = 8X

⇒ X = 234 / 8

⇒ X = 29.25

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: A negative sign in magnification of spherical mirrors indicates that the _______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**image is real**__.

__
 
• The **negative sign** in the magnification of spherical mirrors indicates that the **image formed is inverted**.
 
• In the case of mirrors, an **inverted image** is always a **real image**.
 
• A **real image** is formed when the reflected rays actually meet at a point.
 
• Convex mirrors always produce **virtual, erect, and diminished images**, but concave mirrors can produce real or virtual images depending on the object’s position.
 
• When the object is placed beyond the **focal point** of a concave mirror, the image formed is real and inverted, leading to a **negative magnification**.
 
• The **magnification formula** is: **m = -v/u**, where **v** is the image distance, **u** is the object distance, and the negative sign denotes the inverted (real) image.
 
• This concept is crucial in applications such as **optical instruments, telescopes, and projectors**, which utilize real images.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Image is diminished**__

 __
 
• A diminished image is smaller than the object.
 
• It is typically formed by **convex mirrors** and some specific cases of concave mirrors.
 
• Diminished images are usually virtual, although real images can also be diminished in specific setups.
 
 
 
• **Image is enlarged**__
 __
 
• An enlarged image is larger than the object.
 
• It is often formed by a **concave mirror** when the object is placed between the focal point and the mirror.
 
• Such images are usually virtual, although real images can also be enlarged in particular cases.
 
 
 
• **Image is virtual**__
 
 
• A virtual image is formed when the reflected rays do not actually meet but appear to meet when extended backward.
 
• Virtual images are always **erect** and are commonly produced by **plane mirrors, convex mirrors,** and concave mirrors under specific conditions.
 
• Virtual images cannot be projected onto a screen.

questions.question: Find the magnitude of applied force on a box of mass 10 kg for 20 s. It increases the box's velocity from 5 m s⁻¹ to 15 m s⁻¹?.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**5 N**__.

__
 
• The formula to calculate the **force** is derived from Newton's second law of motion: **F = ma**, where **F** is the force, **m** is the mass of the object, and **a** is the acceleration.
 
• Here, the mass of the box is given as **10 kg**.
 
• To find acceleration, we use the formula: **a = (v - u)/t**, where:
 
 
• **v** = final velocity = **15 m/s**
 
• **u** = initial velocity = **5 m/s**
 
• **t** = time = **20 s**
 
 
 
• Substituting the values:
 
 
• **a = (15 - 5)/20 = 10/20 = 0.5 m/s²**
 
 
 
• Now, substituting **m = 10 kg** and **a = 0.5 m/s²** into the formula **F = ma**:
 
 
• **F = 10 × 0.5 = 5 N**
 
 
 
• Thus, the **magnitude of the applied force** is **5 N**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Methane, on burning with oxygen, gives which of the following products?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Methane** (CH₄) is a simple hydrocarbon and the main component of natural gas.
 
• When methane burns in the presence of sufficient oxygen, it undergoes **complete combustion**.
 
• The chemical reaction for complete combustion of methane is: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.
 
• This reaction produces **carbon dioxide** (CO₂) and **water vapor** (H₂O) as the primary products.
 
• Complete combustion releases a large amount of **energy**, making methane an efficient fuel.
 
• Carbon dioxide and water produced are gases at standard temperature and pressure, with water mostly in vapor form due to the heat of combustion.
 
• In the absence of sufficient oxygen, incomplete combustion may occur, producing carbon monoxide (CO) and soot, but this is not the typical reaction when methane burns properly.
 
• Methane combustion is widely used for heating, cooking, and electricity generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Carbonic Acid**__

 __
 
• Carbonic acid (H₂CO₃) forms when carbon dioxide dissolves in water.
 
• It is an intermediate in the carbon cycle but is not a direct product of methane combustion.
 
• Carbonic acid plays a key role in ocean acidification but is unrelated to the burning of methane.
 
 
 
• **Carbon monoxide and water**__
 __
 
• Carbon monoxide (CO) is produced during incomplete combustion due to insufficient oxygen.
 
• Incomplete combustion is hazardous because CO is a poisonous gas.
 
• Complete combustion of methane ideally avoids producing CO.
 
 
 
• **Carbon monoxide only**__
 
 
• Carbon monoxide is never the sole product of methane combustion.
 
• It appears only in incomplete combustion scenarios along with other products like soot and water vapor.

questions.question: 18 boys and 24 girls can complete a piece of work in 16 days. All of them started working together but after 12 working days, all girls and 6 boys stopped working. 12 boys completed the remaining work in 9 days. How many days will it take to complete the entire job if only 24 girls have to complete the job?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

18 boys and 24 girls can complete the work in 16 days.

After 12 days, all girls and 6 boys stopped working.

Remaining 12 boys completed the remaining work in 9 days.

We need to find how many days 24 girls alone would take to complete the job.

**Formula used:**

Work done per day = Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Total work = (18 boys + 24 girls) × 16 days

Let efficiency of 1 boy = B and 1 girl = G

So, (18B + 24G) × 16 = Total work

Work done in first 12 days = (18B + 24G) × 12

Remaining work = Total work - Work done in 12 days

Remaining work = (18B + 24G) × (16 - 12)

Remaining work = (18B + 24G) × 4

This remaining work is completed by 12 boys in 9 days:

Work by 12 boys in 9 days = 12B × 9

⇒ (18B + 24G) × 4 = 12B × 9

⇒ 72B + 96G = 108B

⇒ 96G = 36B

⇒ G = (36/96)B

⇒ G = (3/8)B

Now, total work = (18B + 24G) × 16

Substituting G = (3/8)B

⇒ (18B + 24 × 3/8 B) × 16

⇒ (18B + 9B) × 16

⇒ 27B × 16

⇒ Total work = 432B

Work done by 24 girls per day = 24G

⇒ 24 × (3/8)B

⇒ 9B

Time taken by 24 girls to complete total work:

⇒ 432B / 9B = 48 days

**∴ 24 girls alone will complete the work in 48 days.**

questions.question: An electric lamp, whose resistance is 10 Ω, and a conductor of 2 Ω resistance are connected to a 24 V battery in series. Then the current through the circuit will be ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**2 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The total resistance in the circuit can be calculated since the resistor values are in **series.**
 
• For resistors connected in series, the total resistance is the **sum of individual resistances.**
 
• Here, the resistance of the electric lamp is **10 Ω**, and the conductor has a resistance of **2 Ω.**
 
• Total resistance, **R = 10 Ω + 2 Ω = 12 Ω.**
 
• The voltage of the battery is given as **24 V.**
 
• Using **Ohm’s Law (V = IR),** the current through the circuit can be calculated:
 
 
• **I = V / R**
 
• Substituting the values, **I = 24 V / 12 Ω = 2 A.**
 
 
 
• Thus, the current flowing through the circuit is **2 A.**
 
• This is why the correct answer is **2 A.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:**

 
 
• It states that the **current (I)** flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the **voltage (V)** across its ends, provided the temperature and other physical conditions remain constant.
 
• The formula is expressed as **V = IR,** where R is the resistance.
 
 
 
• **Series Circuit:**
 
 
• In a series circuit, the total resistance is the **sum of all individual resistances.**
 
• The current remains the **same** through all components in a series circuit.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Used in **calculating resistance, current,** or voltage in electrical circuits.
 
• Helpful in designing **electrical and electronic circuits.**

Let the increased working hours be H + X.

100 : 75 = H : (H + X)

100/75 = (H + X)/H

4/3 = (H + X)/H

H + X = (4/3)H

X = (4/3)H - H

X = (1/3)H
